title: Energy for Earth Processes: Heat, Albedo and the Greenhouse Effect

key_big: Internal heat drives plates; the Sun drives weather and climate.
key_sub: If more energy comes in than goes out, Earth warms.
body_html:
How to think about it

Earth's interior is heated by radioactive decay and heat left from its formation; this heat drives mantle convection and plate tectonics. The Sun supplies far more energy at the surface, driving weather, ocean currents and the water cycle.

About 30% of sunlight is reflected (Earth's albedo is about 0.3). The rest is absorbed and re-emitted as infrared. Greenhouse gases absorb some of this infrared and send part of it back down, keeping Earth about 33 °C warmer than it would otherwise be.

Example

A surface reflects 240 W/m² of 300 W/m². Albedo?

240 ÷ 300

Answer: 0.80

Example

Incoming 340 W/m², outgoing 339 W/m². What happens?

1 W/m² more comes in than goes out

Answer: Earth slowly warms

Common mistakes

  • Saying the greenhouse effect is caused by the ozone hole.
  • Thinking the Equator is hotter because it is closer to the Sun.
  • Saying Earth's internal heat drives the weather.

faq.q: Why do dark surfaces warm faster?
faq.a: They have a low albedo, so they absorb most of the sunlight that falls on them instead of reflecting it.
The natural greenhouse effect is essential: without it Earth would average about −18 °C. The problem is the enhanced greenhouse effect from extra greenhouse gases added by people.

items.q: What is latent heat's role in weather?

items.e: Tropical cyclones are fuelled by latent heat.
